what: Unilever sells everyday consumer products in most countries: Dove and Vaseline in personal care, Domestos and Omo in home care, Hellmann's and Knorr in food, and Magnum and Ben & Jerry's in ice cream, which it is separating into a standalone company.
customers: Consumers worldwide through supermarkets, small shops and e-commerce, with a large share of sales in emerging markets.
money: hair care, skin care and vitamins
Dove, Rexona, Axe and oral care
moat: Brands people ask for by name, shelf space in millions of shops, and distribution in emerging markets built over a century.
risks: Growth has depended heavily on price increases rather than volume
Supermarket own-label products take share when household budgets tighten
Currency moves in emerging markets reduce reported results
The ice cream separation is a large reorganisation while the rest is being restructured
opportunities: Separating ice cream leaves a higher-margin, faster-growing company behind
A cost programme is cutting overheads and reinvesting in the thirty largest brands
Emerging market exposure gives long-term volume growth as incomes rise
watch: Underlying volume growth rather than price, and progress of the ice cream separation.
